blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus told a story about a man who had two sons. The younger one came to his daddy and asked for his share of the inheritance right now, while the old man was still living. And the father divided it between them.

verses.text: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Riotous living, the King James calls it. Money goes fast when you are trying to fill a hole with it. Then a famine came to that land, and he started to be in want. He hired himself out to a man who sent him to feed the hogs. He was so hungry he wanted to eat what the hogs were eating, and nobody gave him a thing.

verses.text: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he came to himself, he said,

segments.speaker: younger-son
segments.text: How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

verses.text: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

segments.speaker: younger-son
segments.text: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

verses.text: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

segments.speaker: younger-son
segments.text: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He came to himself. Some of us know that moment. Not the moment you get fixed. The moment you finally see where you are.

verses.text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at that father. A great way off. That means he was looking. That means he had been watching that road. And he ran to that boy, threw his arms around him, and kissed him. He did not even wait for the speech.

verses.text: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the son said unto him,

segments.speaker: younger-son
segments.text: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

verses.text: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

segments.text: But the father said to his servants,

segments.speaker: father
segments.text: Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

verses.text: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

segments.speaker: father
segments.text: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

verses.text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

segments.speaker: father
segments.text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When I say he was lost, you say, and is found. He was lost. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "And is found"] And is found. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "He was lost"] That is a father’s joy.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: But there is another son in this story. The elder son was out in the field, and when he came near the house he heard music and dancing. When he found out why, he got angry and would not go in. So the father went out to him too.

verses.text: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he answering said to his father,

segments.speaker: elder-son
segments.text: Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

verses.text: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

segments.speaker: father
segments.text: Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

verses.text: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

segments.speaker: father
segments.text: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That father went out to both of his sons. One came home from a far country. One was standing right outside the door. The story ends before we find out if the elder son went in. Maybe that is on purpose. Whichever son you are tonight, the story shows a father who comes out to meet them both.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 15:11-32; no claim about the listener's standing; ends on the father going to both sons.

cultural.note: Plain and warm; 'hogs' is everyday speech; the elder son is not mocked.
